page: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.6xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the high clock speed instance family. Built on KVM hypervisor architecture, this instance integrates 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs utilizing Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors operating at 3.4 GHz. System memory is provisioned at 48.0 GiB, providing an exact allocation of 2.0 GiB of RAM per core. This 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes computational throughput over large memory footprints.

From an I/O and infrastructure perspective, the ecs.hfc9i.6xlarge includes an 18 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile to manage inter-service communication and remote transfers. The server contains no integrated local storage and includes zero bundled public IPv4 addresses, requiring instances to utilize cloud block storage services for file systems and network address translation or Elastic IPs for external access. In addition, the configuration excludes GPU accelerators, narrowing the architecture strictly to central processor tasks.

Qualitatively, the resource allocation provides balanced cost efficiency for tasks requiring rapid clock frequencies without the expense of unneeded storage media or surplus memory capacity. The instance is suitable for compute-bound engineering workloads, including software compilation, automated continuous integration and testing environments, data transformation pipelines, and parallel batch processing jobs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the high clock speed family, designed for workloads requiring substantial processing capability and modest memory allocations. Powered by 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs from the Intel Xeon 6982P-C series running at a base clock speed of 3.4 GHz, the instance delivers sustained compute performance on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 48.0 GiB of RAM, maintaining a strict 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GiB per virtual core. The server includes no local disk storage, necessitating remote storage volumes for persistent data operations, and provides a network baseline throughput of 18 Gbps. Because it eliminates the overhead of attached physical storage and hardware accelerators, it offers focused cost efficiency for compute-dense scenarios. The ecs.hfc9i.6xlarge is appropriate for compute-heavy batch processing, code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, video transcoding, and scientific simulation tasks where high frequency and raw CPU execution speed are paramount.
